title: terrarium
subtitle: generative music in a jar, for monome norns
about: A tiny world that makes music on its own. Weather falls on a landscape inside a jar, and every drop plays a note where it lands. Press Start sound and just listen, or reach in and change what lives there. Nothing you do can break it.
more: terrarium is a script for monome norns, a small computer for making sound. What plays here is the real script, running in your browser with the same Mutable Instruments sound code a norns plays. You don't need to know anything about music or synthesizers: each part of the jar has just two knobs, and the screen shows pictures, not numbers.

actions.label: Shuffle
actions.title: A whole new terrarium: random parts, knobs and settings

gallery_intro: Five parts, each a piece of the scene relating to the sound. Turn E1 to pick the part, press K2 to swap what lives there.

gallery.title: weather
gallery.text: When notes happen: rain, lightning or snow. Where a drop lands sets its pitch.

gallery.title: soil
gallery.text: What grows from the ground plays the notes: a meadow, crystals or reeds.
gallery.alt: A meadow of flowers growing along the ground

gallery.title: water
gallery.text: A pond or a fog that colors the sound as it passes through.
gallery.alt: A pond rippling below the ground line

gallery.title: air
gallery.text: The sky, where the sound rings out: clouds, fireflies or mountains.

gallery.title: hum
gallery.text: A low drone under it all, always there: an aurora or deep roots.
gallery.alt: An aurora shimmering at the top of the sky

controls.does: pick a part of the jar: weather, soil, water, air or hum
shape that part; the two knobs show their names while you turn them
swap what lives there (rain for snow, a meadow for crystals…)
a gesture: a new tune, a strike, freeze the sky, hush the hum
choose a variety of what lives there
peek at the whole jar; E2 picks a setting and E3 changes it
a whole new terrarium, at random (the Shuffle button does it too)
